papers.title_in_file: Efficient Encodings of the Travelling Salesperson Problem for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.what_it_is: Simulation study comparing QUBO, HOBO and permutation encodings of the TSP under QAOA and VQE.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in numerical simulation, the permutation encoding produced more feasible solutions and solutions closer to the optimum than the QUBO and HOBO encodings.
quotes: The permutation encoding strongly benefits from its inability to create infeasible solutions, outperforming both the QUBO and HUBO encoding.
It produces more feasible solutions and solutions that are closer to the optimum compared to the other two encodings.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their recommendation of the permutation encoding rests on results for instances up to 6 nodes and that it remains an open question whether its good performance is due to the small problem size.
quotes: Generally speaking, based on the results we obtained for instances up to 6 nodes, we recommend the permutation encoding of the TSP due to its clear advantages in performance.
However, it remains an open question whether the good performance of the permutation encoding is due to the small problem size.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its own results (Discussion, p.6).

assertions.value: The authors state that there is no known efficient calculation of a Hamiltonian for the permutation encoding, which limits it to algorithms such as VQE where no Hamiltonian is necessary.
quotes: However, there is no known efficient calculation of a Hamiltonian for the permutation encoding. This drawback limits the method to being used alongside algorithms like VQE, where no Hamiltonian is necessary.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own method (Conclusions, p.5).

papers.title_in_file: Explainable quantum regression algorithm with encoded data structure
papers.what_it_is: Constructs a variational quantum regression algorithm whose parameters map to regression coefficients, with a classically emulated numerical test.

assertions.value: The authors construct a variational quantum regression algorithm in which the quantum state encodes the classical data table and the variational parameters correspond to the regression coefficients.
quotes: In this paper, we construct the first interpretable quantum regression algorithm, in which the quantum state exactly encodes the classical data table and the variational parameters correspond directly to the regression coefficients
assertions.certainty_reason: Construction and claim of interpretability by the authors; not an independent test.

assertions.value: The authors state that, with compressed encoding, the read-out error is exponentially suppressed compared with one-hot encoding.
quotes: For compressed encoding, the read-out error δϵ(L, M ) equals (NL + NM )δM , exponentially suppressed (due to NL, NM ≪ NQ) than the one-hot encoding.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived by the authors in the paper; the derivation was not checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical training was emulated classically, in one setup with 13 qubits.
quotes: we can emulate classically the quantum regression training with 13 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its numerical results were produced (Numerical results, p.18).

assertions.value: The authors state that deterministic and non-uniform state preparation is still costly at large data limits and that they mitigate this with bootstrap samples.
quotes: Although deterministic and non-uniform state preparation is still costly at large data limits (see Appendix D), we mitigate this problem by replacing master data training with bootstrap samples
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit (Conclusion, p.22).

papers.title_in_file: Radio Signal Classification by Adversarially Robust Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, dataset and encoding sections, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Simulation study of quantum variational classifiers on radio-signal classification under adversarial attacks, compared with CNNs.

assertions.value: The authors report in simulation that attacks generated on QVCs transfer well to CNN models, while QVCs primarily resist attacks generated on CNNs.
quotes: Our extensive simulation results present that attacks generated on QVCs transfer well to CNN models, indicating that these adversarial examples can fool neural networks that they are not explicitly designed to attack. However, the converse is not true. QVCs primarily resist the attacks generated on CNNs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they sample 5000 data points per class for training and 500 per class for testing.
quotes: Specifically, we sample 5000 data points per class for training and 500 per class for testing.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that amplitude encoding is well known to require large circuit depths, and report that encoding their input data needs almost 1000 gates on average.
quotes: Although amplitude encoding offers a highly efficient way of encoding data for QML, it is a well-known limitation that such encoding schemes require large circuit depths to implement.
The average number of gates necessary for encoding our input data is almost 1000
assertions.certainty_reason: General limitation attributed to prior work; the gate count is the authors' own figure.

papers.title_in_file: Towards Quantum Graph Neural Networks: An Ego-Graph Learning Approach
papers.version_note: File name says Decompositional-Quantum-Graph-Neural-Network (arXiv 2201.05158); the file content is v3, retitled 'Towards Quantum Graph Neural Networks: An Ego-Graph Learning Approach', the same arXiv id as the record.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes egoQGNN, a hybrid quantum-classical graph neural network, run on a classical simulator.

assertions.value: The authors report that egoQGNN outperforms competitive state-of-the-art models with only 1.68% parameters compared to those models.
quotes: Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms competitive state-of-the-art models with only 1.68% parameters compared to those models.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, authors' claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method is implemented using the OriginQ simulator on a classical computer.
quotes: The proposed method is implemented using the OriginQ [61] simulator on a classical computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its experiments were run.

assertions.value: The authors list achieving exponential speed-up with quantum techniques as a long-term goal.
quotes: a long-term goal, quantum techniques need to be utilized to achieve exponential speed-up.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement of future work; not shown in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Scalability Challenges in Variational Quantum Optimization under Stochastic Noise
papers.what_it_is: Numerical scaling study of classical optimizers on noisy variational loss functions for random QUBO instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that the critical noise threshold for successful optimization decreases rapidly as system size grows, and that the required measurement shots quickly become impractical.
quotes: We find that the critical noise threshold for successful optimization decreases rapidly as system size grows.
Translating these thresholds into required measurement shots reveals that achieving sufficient precision in the evaluated loss values quickly becomes impractical, even for moderately-sized problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study how classical optimizers minimize variational quantum loss functions for random QUBO instances, with uncertainty modeled as effective Gaussian noise.
quotes: We systematically investigate this scaling behavior by analyzing how classical optimizers minimize variational quantum loss functions for random QUBO instances in the presence of uncertainty, modeled as effective Gaussian noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope (Abstract).

assertions.value: The authors state that their experimental data are limited by the computational cost of simulating larger system sizes, so conclusions about exact scaling need cautious analysis.
quotes: Given the limited experimental data – constrained by the computational cost of simulating larger system sizes – any conclusions about the exact scaling behaviors or asymptotic trends require cautious analysis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own data.

papers.title_in_file: Machine learning of reduced quantum channels on NISQ devices
papers.what_it_is: Neural-network method that learns an effective quantum channel, tested on simulated data and on the ibmq ehningen processor.

assertions.value: The authors report that, using data from the NISQ device, they can efficiently infer a quantum channel that accurately captures qubit cross-talk in the inspected circuit.
quotes: Using data generated by the NISQ device, we can nevertheless efficiently infer a quantum channel, which accurately captures qubit cross-talk in the inspected circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one device and circuit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Markovian assumption limits the method's ability to capture generic evolutions.
quotes: On the one hand, while we can train the network using any dynamics, this assumption clearly represents a limitation on its ability to capture generic evolutions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the device experiment used the 27-qubit ibmq ehningen processor with 20 000 shots in each of 9 Pauli bases.
quotes: In the following, we explore quantum channels that are implemented on the 27-qubit ibmq ehningen NISQ processor.
We run a total of 20 000 shots in each of the 9 necessary Pauli bases.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

papers.title_in_file: Generating Approximate Ground States of Molecules Using Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: Generative QML model (classical network driving a variational circuit) for ground states across a molecular potential energy surface, with proven lower bounds.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with a small number of training examples, a simple quantum neural network generated approximate ground states with fidelity greater than 99% in most of the cases considered.
quotes: We observe that even given a small number of training examples, we can construct a simple quantum neural network that is capable of generating the approximate groundstate of the molecules with ﬁdelity greater than 99% in most of the cases considered.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on small benchmark molecules.

assertions.value: The authors prove that learning across an avoided crossing from a small number of samples would violate Grover's lower bound.
quotes: From a theoretical perspective, we further prove limitations on these protocols by showing that if we were able to learn across an avoided crossing using a small number of samples, then we would be able to violate Grover’s lower bound.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sec. IV A, Grover Search Lower Bound (proof not re-derived by the reader).

assertions.value: The authors state that the scalability of the method and the existence of barren plateaus remain open questions, with potential issues from vanishing gradients.
quotes: First, there is the question of scalability of the method and question about the existence of barren plateaus in the optimization landscape.

While the numerical experiments provided give evidence that the presented ideas work in practice, at least in some test cases, there are potential issues due to vanishing gradients arising during training.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit (Conclusion).

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Neural Networks (VQNNS) in Image Classification
papers.what_it_is: Short paper training a quantum neural network with a QAOA-style variational layer on MNIST and a crack-image dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQNN takes less time than QNN on the surface-crack experiment, with improved accuracy (figures are in their Table 1).
quotes: The results are shown in the below Table 1 which shows that VQNN is taking less time than QNNs for the experiment with detecting surface cracks with an imporoved accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small study; the numbers are only in a table.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MNIST subset holds 200 images of hand written 0 and 1 digits and that the crack dataset has 1,000 images per class, 2,000 in total.
quotes: MNIST dataset contains 200 images from the training sample which contains hand written 0 and 1 digits.
Each class has 1,000 images for a total of 2,000 images.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset setup.

assertions.value: The authors state they restricted themselves to limited sized sample datasets and did not incorporate phase oracles in the ansatz circuit.
quotes: In this research work, we have restricted ourselves up to a limited sized sample datasets.
Also, we haven’t incorporated any phase oracles in the ansatz circuit for better entanglement.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states these limits (Conclusion).
